skill.name: face-swap
skill.description: Swap a face / character into video or images on RunComfy via the `runcomfy` CLI. Routes across community Wan 2-2 Animate (audio-driven character animation + identity swap), GPT Image 2 Edit (single-shot precise face swap on still images via reference composition), Nano Banana Edit (batch identity-preserving swap), Flux Kontext (single-ref high-fidelity local face edit), and Kling 2-6 Motion Control Pro (transfer motion from one performance onto a target character). Picks the right model for the user's actual intent — single still vs video, full character vs face only, dialog scene vs silent motion. Triggers on "face swap", "swap face", "deepfake", "face replacement", "character swap", "head swap", "put X's face on Y", "make this video star X", "replace the actor in this video", "swap the character in the photo", "deepfake video", "ReActor alternative", or any explicit ask to substitute one identity for another.
skill.summary: Choose a RunComfy model for still image face edits, character animation, or motion transfer.
skill.author: prime-skills

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown formatting, reference links, or normal CLI token storage. The audit identified unpinned installs, unsafe shell construction guidance, and gaps in consent for cloud processing and audio reuse. No evidence of system reconnaissance, credential exfiltration, or an audit-directed prompt injection was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pass serialized JSON as a separate argument through a shell-free process interface. Do not insert user text directly into shell source.
Pin the reviewed CLI release and skill revision. Explain global changes and require separate user approval before installing anything.
Disclose the service, inputs, and applicable retention terms. Ask for approval before submission and limit media access to approved assets.

remediation.issue: Speaker consent and synthetic media disclosure
remediation.suggestion: Check permission from the people depicted and heard, including speakers whose recordings are reused. Require appropriate labels before sharing edited media.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Parsing Before JSON Validation
semantic_findings.description: The examples put model inputs inside shell strings. If an agent inserts untrusted text directly, the shell can interpret it before RunComfy sees the JSON.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples use inline shell quoting, but the security note rules out injection based only on CLI behavior. No unsafe execution was observed.

semantic_findings.title: Global Skill Installation Outside Declared Tool Scope
semantic_findings.description: The setup guide instructs global installation from a community repository without pinning a revision. This can expose future agent sessions to separately sourced instructions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The global installation command is explicit. It uses a different tool than the RunComfy-only execution scope stated later.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Media Transfer Without Explicit Cloud Approval
semantic_findings.description: RunComfy receives prompts and media URLs and fetches assets for processing. The consent checklist does not require approval for cloud processing or explain retention.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source documents API submission and asks about media rights. It does not require separate approval for third-party processing or state retention terms.

semantic_findings.title: Original Audio Reuse Without Checking Speaker Consent
semantic_findings.description: The spokesperson example pairs a new face with the original audio. The checklist does not explicitly verify permission from the recorded speaker for that reuse.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly reuses original audio. The checklist covers source asset rights and the replacement face, but does not separately address speaker consent.

content.user_title: Swap Faces in Images and Videos
content.value_statement: Still image edits, dialogue animation, and motion transfer need different inputs. This skill selects a RunComfy model for your media and editing goal.
actual_capabilities: Animate a character portrait using an audio track with Wan 2-2 Animate.
Transfer motion from a performance video to a target character image with Kling Motion Control.
Assign scene and identity references for a still image face edit with GPT Image 2 Edit.
Use a shared identity reference across several scene images with Nano Banana 2 Edit.
Describe a face change for a single source image without a separate identity image using Flux Kontext Pro.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, an authenticated account, and network access to the cloud service.
The Wan route animates a portrait from audio. It does not preserve the motion of an existing video.
The models may change details outside the requested region. Exact likeness and timing are not guaranteed.
The skill does not enforce consent, apply disclosure labels, or run full ComfyUI node workflows through these routes.

use_cases.title: Revise a Product Gallery
use_cases.description: Use the same approved identity reference across several product images. Review each result for changes to the product and scene.

use_cases.title: Animate a Fictional Narrator
use_cases.description: Create a labeled narration clip from an original character portrait and a recording approved by the speaker.

use_cases.title: Test Character Motion
use_cases.description: Apply a consenting performer's reference movement to a fictional character for an animation preview.

prompt_templates.title: Edit One Still Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the approved illustration as the source. Describe a face edit for a fictional character while keeping the pose and background. Ask before submitting it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: one source image and no identity reference.

prompt_templates.title: Assign Scene and Identity References
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my first approved image as the scene and the second as the fictional identity reference. Keep the pose, clothes, and lighting. Ask before processing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Consistent Gallery Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my fictional identity reference and approved gallery images fit one request. Keep the same output dimensions and show the proposed inputs before submission.
prompt_templates.scenario: Multiple images with a common identity and output size.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Video Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare motion transfer and audio-driven animation for my fictional character. I have an approved performance clip and narration. Choose a route after confirming my priority.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: choose between preserving a performance and animating to dialogue.

output_examples.input: Plan a face edit for one approved illustration without a second portrait.
output_examples.output: Suggested route: Flux Kontext Pro. The illustrated scene is the only input. Review pose, lighting, and background after generation. No media was submitted.

output_examples.input: Keep the movement from my approved performance clip and apply it to a fictional character.
output: Suggested route: Kling Motion Control. Use your performance video for motion and your character image for appearance.
Review body movement and framing in the preview. Label the resulting clip before sharing.

output_examples.input: Use one approved fictional identity reference across three scene images.
output_examples.output: Suggested route: Nano Banana 2 Edit. Use one identity reference and three scene images. Check all outputs for consistent identity, framing, and lighting.

best_practices: Confirm consent from the people depicted or heard, and approve the cloud submission before sharing media URLs.
State which asset supplies the identity, scene, motion, or audio. Specify which details must remain unchanged.
Review generated media before use and apply the disclosure required by your publication platform.
anti_patterns: Do not use a real person's face or voice without permission or present synthetic media as genuine.
Do not paste long-lived media access links or account tokens into edit prompts.
Do not choose audio-driven animation when preserving specific movements from a source video is essential.

faq.question: Does this skill process media locally?
faq.answer: No. The RunComfy CLI submits the model request to a cloud service and downloads the result.

faq.question: What do I need before starting?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI, authenticate your account, and prepare approved media URLs for the selected route.

faq.question: Can I edit a face without a reference portrait?
faq.answer: Yes. Flux Kontext Pro can use a description for a single image edit. It cannot verify likeness to a specific person.

faq.question: Which route preserves an existing performance?
faq.answer: Use Kling Motion Control with a reference video and target character image. Review the result because motion fidelity can vary.

faq.question: Can I use one identity reference for several scenes?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented Nano Banana route accepts up to 20 inputs per request, including the identity reference.

faq.question: Does the skill check consent or label the results?
faq.answer: No. Confirm permission for faces, voices, and source media, and follow platform disclosure rules before sharing.
